newsitem.title: USA: News Corp. declines comment on Pointcast takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: News Corp. declines comment on Pointcast takeover talk.

text.p: News Corp. Tuesday declined to comment on a report that it was in talks to acquire privately held Internet broadcaster Pointcast Inc.

Citing sources familiar with the deal, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that News Corp. had offered between $350 million and $450 million for Cupertino, Calif.-based Pointcast, an Internet start-up widely viewed as a hot initial public offering prospect.
"The problem is that this is something I can't comment on," a News Corp. spokesman said of the Pointcast speculation.
"Like all business deals or non-business deals, we can't comment," he said.
The report followed a denial by Pointcast's top executive Monday of rumours among Internet industry analysts that the company was in talks to be acquired by the global media giant.
"That's a rumour. There are no facts behind that," Pointcast Chief Executive Christopher Hassett told Reuters Monday.
However, he did not deny the possibility of an initial public offering of the company's shares.
"Our intent is not to remain private," Hassett said. "An IPO is definitely a possibility in the near future."

Currently, News Corp.'s primary Internet initiative in the United States is its TV Guide Entertainment Network, a Web site offering a variety of entertainment content, anchored by the TV listings magazine.
